pr_title: drivers: pwm_nrfx: Refactor pwm_set_cycles to fix on/off issues
pr_body:
This commits refactors implementation of the pwm_set_cycles function
to fix the following issues:
- when a channel was already set with a non-zero pulse width, setting
  cycles for another one required specifying a matching period value,
  even if that value was to be ignored anyway when the channel was to
  be set to constant inactive or active level; due to this limitation,
  it was not possible to e.g. use the LED driver API and turn off a LED
  while another one (within the same PWM instance) was blinking
- the above limitation also applied when a channel was set with a pulse
  width equal to period (duty 100%); even though such channel was not
  in fact using the PWM peripheral, other channels within the same PWM
  instance were forced to use the same period
- after a PWM generation was started for a channel, it was not possible
  to change its pulse width before two PWM periods passed (while it
  should be possible to change it after every period); this was caused
  by a looping mechanism that was unnecessarily activated in the PWM
  peripheral

Fixes #47854.
pr_comments:
Indeed. I managed to mess it up. 🤦
Here's a fix: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/48352.

issue_context.title: Multiple blinking LED's cannot be turned off

review_comments: i wonder if we need to care about potential race condition here? What if there is a context switch here and another channel is set. In that case stop is initiated but `stop_requested` flag is not set. Second channel will not pend until pwm is stopped. What are the consequences?

In consequence, a playback request made before the PWM actually stopped would be ignored.
But I don't think we should bother. The driver is not (and never was) thread-safe anyway.
is `seq_values` being used only to determine if pwm is used? If yes then it would be simpler to store bit flags. Check would be faster, less ram, etc.

No, the values determine pulse widths for particular channels. See this part:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/89928afbe8ef0eb4a6a4c45146001f112c1ec800/drivers/pwm/pwm_nrfx.c#L168-L172

For channels that are set to constant inactive or active level we have here 0 or `PWM_NRFX_CH_COMPARE_MASK`, respectively, what means that such channel does not need to be driven by the PWM peripheral, and that's what the `channel_needs_pwm` function checks.

i didn't notice that it's used by the nrfx driver by assigning `.seq.values.p_raw = pwm_nrfx_##idx##_data.seq_values,`
but still, maybe it would be worth to create `uint8_t` mask in the data structure (it would fit without increasing the size) and track use of pwm there. Check would be simplified to just mask against 0.

I'm not convinced it would actually be an improvement. This information would need to be maintained in two places then. I still need to provide proper values in the `seq_values` array for those constant channels. Although they do not need the PWM peripheral, they will still be driven by it when the peripheral is required for any other channel.

i won't insist. Though, imo it would be. There is one if/else which would set/clear flags: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/89928afbe8ef0eb4a6a4c45146001f112c1ec800/drivers/pwm/pwm_nrfx.c#L152 and then `any_other_channel_needs_pwm` become instant.
Okay, now I see it (a bit late, though :wink:). I'll improve this in a follow-up PR.
